stem: Which FDA device class carries the lowest risk?
explanation: Correct: Class I. (see source)

stem: Which controls apply to a Class II medical device?
explanation: Correct: General Controls plus Special Controls. (see source)

stem: Besides risk, FDA device classification depends on which two things?
options: The device's intended use and its indications for use
explanation: Correct: The device's intended use and its indications for use. (see source)

stem: The FDA Quality Management System Regulation amends which part of the Code of Federal Regulations?
explanation: Correct: 21 CFR Part 820. (see source)

stem: Who must give the technician specific written directions for each case?
explanation: Correct: The dentist, through the prescription. (para 1.4.1)

stem: How should a technician treat what they learn about a patient's dental condition or personal life?
options: As privileged information that is not repeated outside professional conversation
As material to share with other patients
As something to post in the lab
explanation: Correct: As privileged information that is not repeated outside professional conversation. (para 1.4.3.3)

stem: Where does the masseter muscle originate?
explanation: Correct: The zygomatic arch. (para 3.21.1)

stem: What is the primary action of the masseter?
options: It elevates, or closes, the mandible
It forms the floor of the mouth
explanation: Correct: It elevates, or closes, the mandible. (para 3.21.1.3)

stem: Where does the medial pterygoid insert?
options: On the neck of the condyloid process
On the medial, or internal, surface of the mandibular ramus
explanation: Correct: On the medial, or internal, surface of the mandibular ramus. (para 3.21.3.2)

stem: What does the orbicularis oris muscle do?
options: It forms the floor of the mouth
explanation: Correct: It closes the lips. (para 3.24)

stem: What is a primary function of the buccinator?
options: Holding food between the teeth while chewing
explanation: Correct: Holding food between the teeth while chewing. (para 3.32.4)

stem: The hamular notch serves as a guide to what?
options: The midline of the mandibular denture
The posterior border of a maxillary denture
The position of the mental foramen
The height of the lower occlusal plane
explanation: Correct: The posterior border of a maxillary denture. (para 3.37.3)

stem: What portion of the palatal vault is made up by the soft palate?
explanation: Correct: The posterior one-third. (para 3.37.4)

stem: What is the vibrating line?
options: The line of flexion between the hard and soft palates
The cutting edge of an anterior tooth
The border of the attached gingiva
The midline of the incisive papilla
explanation: Correct: The line of flexion between the hard and soft palates. (para 3.37.8)

stem: Why do the retromolar pads matter in denture work?
options: They guide the plane of occlusion because their position stays constant after extraction
They form the floor of the mouth
explanation: Correct: They guide the plane of occlusion because their position stays constant after extraction. (para 3.38.2)

stem: The glenoid fossa is found on which bone?
options: The temporal bone, under its zygomatic process
explanation: Correct: The temporal bone, under its zygomatic process. (para 3.43)

stem: During protrusive movement, where do both condyles move?
options: Out of the fossae and onto the articular eminences
explanation: Correct: Out of the fossae and onto the articular eminences. (para 3.44)

stem: How many anterior teeth are in one permanent arch?
explanation: Correct: Six, from canine to canine. (para 4.1.3.2)

stem: Through what opening do nerves and blood vessels enter a tooth?
explanation: Correct: The apical foramen. (para 4.4.4)

stem: What is the lamina dura?
options: A thin, dense layer of bone lining the tooth socket
explanation: Correct: A thin, dense layer of bone lining the tooth socket. (para 4.5.1.2)

stem: What is the difference between free and attached gingiva?
options: Free gingiva is fixed to bone, while attached gingiva moves
Free gingiva can be displaced, while attached gingiva is firmly fixed to the underlying bone
explanation: Correct: Free gingiva can be displaced, while attached gingiva is firmly fixed to the underlying bone. (para 4.5.4)

stem: In the Universal numbering system, which numbers are the maxillary teeth?
explanation: Correct: 1 through 16. (para 4.3)

stem: Medial is a synonym for what term?
explanation: Correct: Internal. (para 3.2.2)

stem: What is the incisal surface?
options: The chewing surface of a posterior tooth
The cutting edge of an anterior tooth
The surface closest to the midline
explanation: Correct: The cutting edge of an anterior tooth. (para 4.7.4-4.7.5)

stem: What is an embrasure?
options: The junction of three crown surfaces
A space that diverges from the contacting proximal surfaces of two adjacent teeth
The cutting edge of an incisor
The opening at the root apex
explanation: Correct: A space that diverges from the contacting proximal surfaces of two adjacent teeth. (para 4.11.2.1)

stem: In an Angle Class III relationship, what profile is typical?
explanation: Correct: A prognathic profile. (para 5.6.3)

stem: On an arcon articulator, where are the condyle elements?
options: On the upper member, with the fossae on the lower member
On the lower member, with the fossae on the upper member, as in the natural anatomy
explanation: Correct: On the lower member, with the fossae on the upper member, as in the natural anatomy. (para 6.7)

stem: What are the three articulator categories by adjustability?
explanation: Correct: Nonadjustable, semiadjustable, and fully adjustable. (para 6.3.3)

stem: What does overmixing gypsum do to its crushing strength?
options: It breaks the forming crystals and reduces strength
explanation: Correct: It breaks the forming crystals and reduces strength. (para 2.5.2)

stem: What is slurry water used for?
options: Accelerating the set of plaster or stone, for example when mounting casts
explanation: Correct: Accelerating the set of plaster or stone, for example when mounting casts. (para 2.6.4.4)

stem: Why should chemical accelerators or retarders never be added to casting or soldering investments?
options: They also reduce setting expansion and crushing strength
They make it impossible to mix
explanation: Correct: They also reduce setting expansion and crushing strength. (para 2.6.4.3)

stem: What is the typical initial set time of dental stone?
explanation: Correct: 8 to 15 minutes. (para 2.10.3)

stem: What are investments composed of?
options: A refractory, such as cristobalite or quartz, plus a binder
explanation: Correct: A refractory, such as cristobalite or quartz, plus a binder. (para 2.12)

stem: What should you do if a gypsum mix in progress seems too thick or thin?
options: Start a new mix rather than adding powder or water
explanation: Correct: Start a new mix rather than adding powder or water. (para 2.17.7)

stem: How long should a phosphate-bonded investment be held under vacuum?
explanation: Correct: 30 seconds. (para 2.17.6)

stem: What are the main components of baseplate wax?
explanation: Correct: Beeswax, paraffin, and coloring. (para 2.22.1)

stem: What is boxing wax used for?
explanation: Correct: Boxing impressions. (para 2.28)

stem: At what temperature is a beeswax dip used to seal refractory casts?
explanation: Correct: 280 to 300 degrees Fahrenheit. (para 2.32)

stem: In heat-cured denture resin, what is the powder?
explanation: Correct: The polymer. (para 2.42)

stem: Why are self-curing resins preferred for denture repair?
options: They are the most elastic liners
The denture does not have to go through a high curing temperature
explanation: Correct: The denture does not have to go through a high curing temperature. (para 2.44.2)

stem: How does the specific gravity of chrome alloys compare with gold?
options: It is about half, so castings are lighter
It is about ten times higher
explanation: Correct: It is about half, so castings are lighter. (para 2.63.2)

stem: What tinfoil thickness is used over the waxed denture?
explanation: Correct: 0.003 inch. (para 2.77.1.2)

stem: What are tinfoil substitutes made of?
options: Sodium or potassium alginate in distilled water
explanation: Correct: Sodium or potassium alginate in distilled water. (para 2.77.2.1)

stem: Which form of flux is best for casting?
explanation: Correct: Powdered flux. (para 2.80.2)

stem: Why is isopropyl alcohol not recommended for the torch?
options: It burns too hot for gold
It smokes badly when applied to wax
explanation: Correct: It smokes badly when applied to wax. (para 2.86)

stem: What is the advantage of sulfuric acid over hydrochloric acid as a pickling solution?
options: It is used to polish acrylic
explanation: Correct: It has no objectionable fumes. (para 2.90)

stem: What is hydrofluoric acid used for in the lab?
explanation: Correct: Dissolving porcelain off metal. (para 2.93)

stem: Which polishing agent is not recommended for acrylic?
options: Rouge, because it collects in crevices around the denture teeth
explanation: Correct: Rouge, because it collects in crevices around the denture teeth. (para 2.100.2)

stem: What is the hardest abrasive known?
explanation: Correct: Diamond. (para 2.100.10)

stem: What flame is suitable for melting chrome alloys?
explanation: Correct: Oxyacetylene. (para 2.102.4.2)

stem: What is the typical melting range of chrome alloys?
explanation: Correct: Over 2600 degrees Fahrenheit. (para 2.102.4.2)

stem: What must be done to gypsum before autoclaving to make improved stone?
options: It is boiled in a 30 percent calcium chloride solution
It is soaked in aqua regia
It is heated in open vats
explanation: Correct: It is boiled in a 30 percent calcium chloride solution. (para 2.11.2)

stem: Is a separator needed when pouring gypsum into impression compound?
explanation: Correct: No. (para 2.34.4)

stem: How should a low-fusing wax impression be rinsed?
options: Carefully with room-temperature water, without touching the tissue side
By scrubbing the tissue side with a brush
explanation: Correct: Carefully with room-temperature water, without touching the tissue side. (para 2.35.2)

stem: Why should condensation silicone impressions be poured promptly?
explanation: Correct: Shrinkage occurs after about 30 minutes. (para 2.37.2.3)

stem: Which hydrocolloid is irreversible?
explanation: Correct: Alginate. (para 2.40)

stem: What happens to a gelled hydrocolloid impression exposed to water or air?
options: It sets harder with no change
explanation: Correct: It changes dimensions. (para 2.40.2.3.1)

stem: Addition silicone and polysulfide impressions should NOT be immersed in which disinfectant?
explanation: Correct: Neutral glutaraldehyde. (para 1.26)

stem: How are polyether impressions disinfected?
options: Like hydrocolloids, by spraying rather than immersion
explanation: Correct: Like hydrocolloids, by spraying rather than immersion. (para 1.27)

stem: From what is slurry dihydrate solution prepared?
options: Freshly set stone that was never poured against a contaminated impression
explanation: Correct: Freshly set stone that was never poured against a contaminated impression. (para 1.31)

stem: When should eye protection be worn?
options: Whenever any possibility of eye damage exists
Only when the supervisor is present
explanation: Correct: Whenever any possibility of eye damage exists. (para 1.10)

stem: What is the rule for running lathes?
options: Never leave them unattended, and turn them off when not in use
Only turn them off at the end of the week
explanation: Correct: Never leave them unattended, and turn them off when not in use. (para 1.15.1)

stem: What is the key infection control concept in the lab?
options: Clean and disinfect contaminated items before they reach the production area
Disinfect items only after they are finished
Disinfect only items that look dirty
Disinfection is done only by the dentist
explanation: Correct: Clean and disinfect contaminated items before they reach the production area. (para 1.20.2)

stem: What is the receiving area?
options: The shipping desk for finished cases
A separate engineering control area for disinfecting incoming items
explanation: Correct: A separate engineering control area for disinfecting incoming items. (para 1.23.1)

stem: What PPE is worn in the receiving area?
options: Gloves, mask, eye protection, and smocks
explanation: Correct: Gloves, mask, eye protection, and smocks. (para 1.24)

stem: How is a finished prosthesis returned to the dentist?
explanation: Correct: Cleaned, disinfected, and bagged. (para 1.30)

stem: Under OSHA, what is an exposure incident?
options: Eye, mouth, mucous membrane, non-intact skin, or parenteral contact with blood or other potentially infectious materials
Breathing room air in the lab
explanation: Correct: Eye, mouth, mucous membrane, non-intact skin, or parenteral contact with blood or other potentially infectious materials. (see source)

source.ref: OSHA Fact Sheet: Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030)

stem: How often is OSHA bloodborne pathogens training given?
options: At assignment, annually, and when tasks change
explanation: Correct: At assignment, annually, and when tasks change. (see source)

source.ref: OSHA Fact Sheet: Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030)

stem: Which HazCom pictogram is used for skin corrosion?
explanation: Correct: Corrosion. (see source)

source.ref: OSHA QuickCard: Hazard Communication Standard Pictogram (OSHA 3491)

stem: Which HazCom pictogram is used for gases under pressure?
explanation: Correct: Gas cylinder. (see source)

source.ref: OSHA QuickCard: Hazard Communication Standard Pictogram (OSHA 3491)
